_schema_note: Key is Coptic 'month-day' (e.g. '12-25' = Mesore 25). Add an entry each time you check Coptic Reader while planning a service. hasHymn should reflect whether the saint has a dedicated entry with hymns on Coptic Reader's Index page.

12-1.name: St. Apoli, Son of Justus
12-1.summary: Martyred in 304 A.D., St. Apoli was a horseman and courageous commander, and crown prince of the Roman Empire, son of Emperor Numerianus. Returning from war to find Diocletian had abandoned the faith and revived pagan worship, Apoli confessed Christ along with his parents Justus and Theoclia and was martyred with them in Alexandria.

12-2.name: St. Pa'esa (Athanasia)
12-2.summary: A 4th-century saint born to wealthy Christian parents in Menouf, known for her charity, prayer, and fasting. After her parents' death she gave away her fortune to the poor, but was later led astray by evil people until the desert fathers sent St. John the Short to guide her back to repentance in the wilderness.

12-3.name: St. Simon (Simeon) the Stylite
12-3.summary: Commemorates the relocation of the body of St. Simon the Stylite in 471 A.D. from the city of Antioch to Constantinople during the reign of Emperor Zeno, in a splendid celebration.

12-3.name: Pope Ebrimus (Primus), Fifth Patriarch of Alexandria
12-3.summary: Born in Alexandria and baptized by St. Mark the Evangelist himself, Ebrimus was one of only three men ordained priests by St. Mark. He was unanimously chosen to succeed Pope Kerdonus and was consecrated in 106 A.D., shepherding the church with special attention to guiding clergy and instructing the flock in Christian manners.

12-4.name: King Hezekiah
12-4.summary: Commemorates the righteous King Hezekiah of Judah, who was healed by God after fervent prayer and given fifteen more years of life (2 Kings 20:1-11). Hezekiah abolished idol worship, destroyed pagan altars, and restored true worship in the temple, reigning 29 years before departing in peace.

12-4.name: St. Anthony the Great (Antonius)
12-4.summary: Commemorates the consecration of the church of St. Anthony, father of all monks, at his monastery in Mount Arabah (Mount Araklio) — a church that still stands today, where monks continue to pray daily. St. Anthony is one of the most significant fathers of monasticism in Coptic tradition.
hymnIds: Doxology for St. Anthony and St. Paul the Hermit together
Praxis Response (consistent with every other saint page checked)

12-5.name: St. John the Soldier
12-5.summary: Born in Ashroubah (Beni Mazar, Minya) to pious Christian parents, John joined the army of the apostate Emperor Julian. While outwardly appearing to persecute Christians alongside his fellow soldiers, he secretly protected and provided for them. When the emperor discovered his account, he had John severely tortured and beheaded, earning the crown of martyrdom.

12-6.name: St. Julietta
12-6.summary: Born in Caesarea, Cappadocia, to wealthy Christian parents, Julietta inherited great wealth which an oppressor tried to defraud from her. When she sought to reclaim it, he accused her of being Christian before the governor, who tortured her and cast her into fire; she delivered her spirit to the Lord and her body remained unharmed by the flames.

12-6.name: St. Jacob al-Baradai (Jacobus Baradaeus)
12-6.summary: Son of a priest from Tela near Edessa, Jacob became a monk in his youth and gained vast knowledge in theology and Syriac/Greek literature. Empress Theodora had him consecrated Metropolitan of Edessa to shepherd Orthodox Christians who rejected the Council of Chalcedon; disguised in a poor beggar's garb (giving rise to his name 'al-Baradai'), he traveled tirelessly ordaining an extraordinary number of clergy — reportedly 100,000 clergy and 89 bishops — before dying at 73 while traveling to meet the Coptic Pope in Egypt.

12-6.name: Abba Besa, Disciple of St. Shenouda the Archimandrite
12-6.summary: Born in the city of Absay to a wealthy, charitable father who prayed for a son and was granted one by God. Educated from age five in reading, writing, and the Scriptures, Besa grew in grace and became a devoted disciple of St. Shenouda the Archimandrite, eventually taking up the monastic life himself.

12-7.name: The Annunciation of the Angel to St. Joachim, with the Birth of the Virgin St. Mary
12-7.summary: God sent the angel Gabriel to announce to St. Joachim the birth of the Virgin Theotokos, St. Mary. Joachim and his wife Anna (Hannah), both from the tribe of Judah and house of David, had been barren for thirty-one years and vowed that if given a child they would dedicate them to the Lord as Samuel was. Gabriel announced that their offspring would bring salvation to the world, and Anna conceived and bore the pure Virgin Mary.

12-8.name: Sts. Eleazar, Salome, and their Seven Children (The Seven Maccabees)
12-8.summary: Martyred in 161 B.C., Eleazar was a descendant of Aaron the priest and a teacher of the Jewish Law who taught his children to keep the Law of Moses. When the Syrian king Antiochus besieged Jerusalem and tried to force the Jewish people to break their fathers' Law, this righteous family refused to comply. Antiochus tortured them severely — flogging, crucifixion, burning, and combing their bodies with metal combs — while Salome encouraged them until all received the crown of martyrdom.

12-9.name: St. Ari (Ori), the Priest of Shatanof
12-9.summary: Martyred in 304 A.D., St. Ari was a priest from Shatanof known for his purity and mercy, gifted by God with healing of the sick and casting out unclean spirits, even foretelling future events by divine inspiration. When the Governor of Nakyos demanded he worship idols, he refused and was severely tortured; Christ appeared to him in prison to heal and strengthen him before he was sent on to further persecution in Alexandria.

12-10.name: St. Pihebs (Bekhibs)
12-10.summary: A soldier from Ashmoon Tanah under the command of Prince Antiochus, Pihebs was summoned along with Anba Klog the bishop, Anba Nehru, and Anba Phillip when it was learned he was Christian. All confessed their faith and were tortured; Pihebs was bound and sent by ship to el-Baramoon, enduring 27 days without food or drink before being severely tortured and finally hacked with a cleaver, receiving the crown of martyrdom. A Christian man retrieved his body and returned it to his hometown.

12-11.name: St. Moisis (Moses), Bishop of Ouseem
12-11.summary: Pure and chaste since his youth, Moisis studied church subjects, was ordained a deacon, then went to the desert of Scetis to become a monk, serving a holy elder for eighteen years with devotion to prayer, fasting, humility, and love. Once his virtues became known, he was consecrated bishop of Ouseem, where he shepherded Christ's flock with great care, remaining ascetic and owning nothing his whole life. He suffered many tribulations alongside Pope Khail I, and God worked many signs and miracles by his hands before he reached old age and departed in peace, having served more than twenty years on his episcopal seat.

12-12.name: Archangel Michael
12-12.summary: The church celebrates the monthly commemoration of the honorable Archangel Michael, through whose intercession God brings the water of the rivers up to its measure and blesses the fruits of the earth and the plants of the field.
hymnIds: Doxology (for Michael alone, and a separate one for Michael and Gabriel)

12-12.name: King Constantine and Queen Helen
12-12.summary: Commemorates the enthronement of Emperor Constantine the Great in Rome in 306 A.D. After his father Constantius Chlorus died, Constantine became emperor and abolished injustice throughout his realm. When the nobles of Rome asked for deliverance from the tyrant Maxentius, Constantine saw a cross in the sky with the words 'With this sign you will conquer,' defeated Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge in 312 A.D., and was received into Rome with great celebration.

12-13.name: Feast of the Transfiguration of Our Lord on Mount Tabor
12-13.summary: One of the minor feasts of our Lord. Jesus took Peter, James, and John up Mount Tabor to pray; His face and robe became radiant, and Moses and Elijah appeared speaking with Him of His departure to be accomplished in Jerusalem. Peter offered to build three tabernacles, but a bright cloud overshadowed them and a voice declared, 'This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear Him,' after which the disciples fell on their faces in fear (Matthew 17:1-8).
hymnIds: Major Feast of the Lord — check Index > Feasts > Transfiguration for the specific hymn set (this page was too slow to load fully to confirm exact titles)

12-14.name: The Great Sign the Lord Manifested During the Papacy of Pope Theophilus
12-14.summary: Commemorates a miracle during the papacy of Pope Theophilus, 23rd Patriarch of Alexandria: a wealthy Jewish man named Philoxinus lived in Alexandria alongside two poor Christian men. When one questioned why the faithful remained poor while an unbeliever prospered, the other explained that worldly riches are not a sign of God's favor. The story illustrates that true faith is tested apart from material wealth — a teaching narrative rather than a saint's biography.

12-15.name: St. Mary Known as Marina, the Ascetic
12-15.summary: An 8th-century saint born Mary to a wealthy Christian father, Euganius, and pious mother, Sarah, in Bithynia, Asia Minor. When her father wished to remarry her off but instead chose monastic life himself, she refused to be left behind, cut her hair, donned men's clothing, and joined him at the monastery disguised as his 'son' Marina. She lived for years undetected among the monks, her gentle voice attributed to her ascetic discipline, persevering in prayer and fasting until her father's death, after which she continued the monastic life as 'the monk Marina.'

12-16.name: The Assumption of the Body of the Virgin St. Mary to Heaven
12-16.summary: Commemorates the revealing of the assumption of the body of St. Mary to heaven. She had departed on the 21st of Tobe, surrounded by the apostles; St. Thomas, absent while preaching in India, arrived after her burial in Gethsemane and was shown her body being taken up by angels. Angelic praises and the aroma of incense surrounded her tomb for three days before her pure body was assumed into heaven.
hymnIds: Major Marian feast — St. Mary the Mother of God has an extensive dedicated Index entry (Psalis, Doxologies, Theotokia, etc.); check Index > Saints > St. Mary the Mother of God for the full set

12-17.name: St. James the Soldier
12-17.summary: Martyred in 304 A.D., James was born in the village of Mengoug to God-fearing Christian parents who had three daughters before him and dedicated him to God in answer to prayer. He tended his father's sheep under a devout shepherd he took as a role model. When persecution arose, the shepherd went to confess Christ, and James asked his father to let him accompany the shepherd to martyrdom.

12-18.name: St. Alexander, Patriarch of Constantinople
12-18.summary: Departed in 336 A.D., an honorable scholar who suffered many hardships opposing the Arian heresy. When St. Athanasius the Apostolic renewed the excommunication of Arius, Emperor Constantine pressured St. Alexander to readmit Arius to communion, but Alexander firmly replied that only the universal council which stripped Arius of his rank could restore it. St. James, Bishop of Nisibis, joined him in prayer that the Lord would keep this danger from the Church.

12-19.name: The Return of the Body of St. Macarius the Great to His Monastery in Scetis
12-19.summary: In 793 A.D., during the papacy of Pope Yoannis IV, the body of St. Macarius the Great was returned to his monastery in Scetis (Wadi El Natrun). It had been away since 480 A.D., when it was moved first to Shabsheer and then to Almay, each city building a great church to house it. Pope Yoannis IV, spending the holy forty days at the saint's monastery, expressed his yearning that the body be returned, and it was accomplished that year.
hymnIds: St. Macarius the Great is a major desert father on Index > Saints > Male Saints with a dedicated hymn set (Psalis, Doxology, etc.) — check there for the full list

12-20.name: The Seven Young Men of Ephesus (Seven Sleepers)
12-20.summary: Martyred around 250 A.D.: Maximus, Malchus, Martinianus, Dionysius, John, Serapion, and Constantine — soldiers of Emperor Decius trusted to guard the royal treasury. When accused of Christianity for refusing idol worship, they hid in a cave outside Ephesus; the emperor had the entrance sealed, delivering their spirits to the Lord. About 200 years later, God revealed their bodies to the bishop of Ephesus in a vision during the reign of Emperor Theodosius the Less, so their story could be a testimony to the resurrection of the dead.

12-21.name: The Commemoration of the Virgin St. Mary, the Mother of God
12-21.summary: The monthly commemoration of the Mother of God, the Virgin St. Mary, intercessor of mankind, the chosen queen, the burning bush, the tabernacle, the pot of manna, Aaron's rod, and the Holy of Holies.
hymnIds: Monthly Marian commemoration — St. Mary has a major dedicated hymn set on Index > Saints > St. Mary the Mother of God (Theotokia, Psalis, etc.)

12-21.name: St. Irene (Eirene)
12-21.summary: A first-century saint, daughter of King Lucianus (Licinius) of Macedonia. She was born after her parents lost all previous children, and her father, concerned for her exceptional beauty, built her a fortified mansion with thirteen maiden servants when she was six. Though her idol-worshiping parents left statues for her to worship, her Christian tutor Apellianus (Aplianus) instructed her wisely and justly instead.

12-22.name: Micah the Prophet
12-22.summary: Departed in 696 B.C.: a righteous Old Testament prophet from the tribe of Judah, born in Moresheth Gath and called Micah el-Morashti. A quiet, wise, and compassionate poet, he prophesied for about sixty years during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, contemporary with the prophet Isaiah. He foretold the destruction of Samaria and Jerusalem, called the people to repentance, and prophesied the return of God's mercy.

12-23.name: The Martyrdom of Thirty Thousand Christians in Alexandria
12-23.summary: Commemorates a massacre following the exile of Pope Dioscorus, 25th Patriarch of Alexandria, by Emperor Marcianus to the island of Gagra. The Chalcedonian Brotarius was appointed patriarch in his place, but the Egyptian bishops refused fellowship with him and convened a council rejecting the Council of Chalcedon and the Tome of Leo. Brotarius, enraged, used government forces to plunder monasteries and churches, growing wealthy, until thieves killed him in the night; the Chalcedonians blamed the followers of Dioscorus, and the furious Emperor sent soldiers who killed about thirty thousand Christians in Alexandria.

12-24.name: St. Thomas, Bishop of Mar'ash (Syria)
12-24.summary: An ascetic worshiper diligent in fasting and prayer, merciful to the poor and needy, consecrated bishop of Mar'ash in Syria for his devoted shepherding. When Diocletian incited persecution against Christians, the governor summoned Thomas and demanded he worship idols; upon his refusal he was severely tortured, had organs dismembered one at a time, and was cast into an abandoned prison for twenty-two years — his congregation presuming him dead — sustained secretly at night by a faithful woman through a small opening in the prison wall, until Emperor Constantine ordered the release of imprisoned Christians.

12-25.name: St. Bessarion the Great
12-25.summary: A 4th-century Egyptian ascetic who trained under Anba Anthony and Anba Macarius before withdrawing into the desert, owning nothing but a coarse garment and the Gospels. Known for walking on water, sweetening salt water for a thirsty companion, healing a paralyzed child, and guiding St. Taor to repentance.

12-25.name: Pope Macarius III, 114th Patriarch of Alexandria
12-25.summary: Born in El-Mahalla El-Koubra, became a monk at St. Pishoy Monastery, served as Bishop of Assiut for 47 years, then Pope of Alexandria from 1944 until his death in 1945. His short papacy included reforms on divorce law, family legislation, and monastic education.

12-26.name: St. Moses (Moisees) and his Sister Sarah
12-26.summary: Martyred in 250 A.D., these two siblings were born to wealthy Christian parents in Alexandria. After their parents' death, Moses gave away all their possessions to the poor rather than marry, and took his sister to a convent of virgins while he withdrew to a nearby mountain in seclusion, the two not seeing each other for ten years, before their eventual martyrdom.

12-27.name: Sts. Benjamin and his sister Eudoxia
12-27.summary: Two siblings born in Shabsheer, Egypt, to pious Christian parents devoted to hospitality and asceticism. Benjamin, longing to shed his blood for Christ, confessed his faith before the governor of Shatanof and was tortured and imprisoned; his sister Eudoxia refused to be separated from him, choosing to die with him rather than leave his side. Both were martyred together after the governor bound them with heavy stones and threw them into the river, from which they were miraculously freed by an angel before ultimately winning their crowns of martyrdom.
